newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka army says 20 Tamil rebels killed in ambush.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka army says 20 Tamil rebels killed in ambush.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops killed up to 20 Tamil Tiger guerrillas in an ambush in the eastern Batticaloa district on Tuesday, a military spokesman said on Thursday.
"Terrorist radio transmission monitored by us revealed that 10 terrorists were killed in the clash," he said. "But our ground troops said at least 20 terrorists were killed."
Troops recovered the body of a rebel along with three rifles at the scene of the ambush at Meeyankulam, about 200 km (125 miles) east of Colombo, he added.
Three soldiers were wounded in the firefight, the spokesman said, but rebel radio, monitored by Reuters, said their fighters killed 10 soldiers.
Troops on a "fighting patrol" in northern Jaffna clashed with a group of rebel infiltrators killing one of them on Wednesday, the spokesman said.
The army was hunting small groups of rebel infiltrators in the Jaffna peninsula, former stronghold of Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, army officials said.
The army ousted the LTTE from Jaffna in April and in September captured Kilinochchi, the last major town under rebel control on the northern mainland.
But the rebels hit back by overrunning the remote Mullaithivu army outpost in July, killing or capturing almost its entire garrison of more than 1,000 men.

Since then the Tigers, who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east, have concentrated on harrassing security forces with hit-and-run attacks launched from their jungle bases.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the rebels' war for independence, now in its 14th year.
Meanwhile, navy patrols fired warning shots to chase Indian trawlers poaching in the island's northwestern waters on Tuesday, a navy spokesman said.
"We detected large-scale poaching by Indian trawlers," he said. "Our patrols chased them away with warning shots."
The incident took place off Talaimannar, 240 km (150 miles) north of Colombo where poaching by trawlers from the south Indian State of Tamil Nadu, across the narrow Palk Strait, was common, he said.
